stocks.note: Numbers as of market close May 27th.
stocks.news:
Goldman Sachs just called for the S&P 500 to grow over 16% this year, a notably bullish revision against the Iran-war and oil-spike backdrop. The Big Tech rotation continues.

Robinhood (HOOD +2.89%) became the first major U.S. retail brokerage to let AI agents open their own accounts and trade stocks with pre-funded wallets. Real-time test of whether retail flow looks the same when the trader is a model. Amazon (AMZN +2.47%) announced it will sell its AI shopping tech to other retailers, who can build their own AI-driven storefronts on top of it. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon (JPM -2.43%) floated a possible $20B acquisition if the right target appears. Abercrombie (ANF +8.88%) crushed earnings expectations even with the Iran war drag on sales.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET May 27th; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com (tracking Brent +2.6%).
economy.commentary:
🛢️ The oil jump is the headline. Brent ripped +2.6% in a single session to $96.74 as Iran's state TV claimed a deal is on the table while U.S. officials publicly contradicted: no deal exists yet. The diplomatic ping-pong matters because the conflict has disrupted roughly 20 million barrels per day, about a fifth of global supply. WTI is sitting at $88.86 today, holding the gains intraday.

The knock-on: France's consumer confidence fell to 82, the lowest reading since March 2023, with the index explicitly blaming U.S.–Iran energy costs. Eurozone risk just got bigger.

Stateside, food prices logged their fastest monthly jump in nearly 4 years in April. Beef hit a record high, tomatoes climbed 33% over the last two months, and the U.S. cattle herd is at a 75-year low. The USDA warns the squeeze could persist as farm production lags demand.

Gold pulled back 1.23% to $4,393 as the dollar firmed on the 10-year tick to 4.51%. The bond market is repricing the inflation-from-energy story in real time.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on May 27th.
crypto.commentary:
A single whale sold $1.29B of IBIT (BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF) in one dark-pool trade Tuesday morning. Dark pools let big players move size without alerting the market. The bigger pattern: spot Bitcoin ETFs have now logged seven straight days of outflows, the second-longest losing streak since they launched in 2024. The institutional bid is unwinding, not just the retail bid.

Structural story: SoFi (SOFI +1.19%) launched SoFiUSD, becoming the first nationally-chartered U.S. bank to put a stablecoin on a public blockchain for everyday customers. Unlike Tether or Circle (CRCL -1.47%), SoFi comes with FDIC insurance, federal oversight, and possibly tokenized deposits that earn interest down the road. Stablecoins are quietly entering the regulated banking stack while the spot crowd cools.

real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage Rates Hit 9-Month High; Refis Collapse; East Bay Board Builds To 2,943 Active (193 New)
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates just touched a 9-month high. The 30-year briefly tagged 6.65% earlier this week, the highest since August 2025, and refi applications fell 18% in a single week as the window slams shut for anyone still hoping to refinance. Insurance is the second squeeze: the typical U.S. home insurance bill jumped 24% to $3,303 a year between 2021 and 2024, with increases in 95% of U.S. ZIP codes. Climate-disaster repricing is now structural, not transitory.

The buyer at your door is rate-aware AND insurance-aware, and today they have more to choose from. The local board expanded: 2,943 active across the East Bay (up 42 from yesterday), 193 new listings (up 22), and 218 closed sales (down 34). New supply outran closings, the first real inventory build of the week.

📍 Alameda & Contra Costa Snapshot (05/28/26)

📍 Fremont: 20 new (up 7 from yesterday's 13).

📍 Union City: 5 new (flat).

📍 Newark: 6 new (up 3).

📍 Hayward: 14 new (flat).

📍 Danville: 15 new (up 5).

📍 Milpitas: 0 new (down 2, quietest on the board).

📍 Oakland: 50 new (down 2 from 52, still volume leader at 786 active).

📍 Livermore: 23 new (up 10, biggest single-city jump).

📍 Castro Valley: 8 new (flat).

📍 Pleasanton: 6 new (down 2).

📍 San Ramon: 21 new (up 5).

📍 Dublin: 12 new (down 2).

📍 Sunol: 1 new (down 1).

📍 San Lorenzo: 5 new (up 1).

📍 San Leandro: 7 new (flat).

The build was broad: Livermore (+10), Fremont (+7), Danville and San Ramon (+5 each) led the supply add. Closed sales cooled to 218 even as new listings climbed, so the board is loosening at the margin.

For agents: the rate-cut buyer isn't coming. The buyer at the door is rate-aware and insurance-aware, and now they have more to choose from. Price for that reality, not for a softer-rate environment that doesn't exist yet.
